messages:
customer_jlewis: Hi team, our Private websocket streams to wss://private-api.redwood.corp/v1/stream are dropping consistently around 60s. Non-streaming REST calls work fine. Started after we put traffic through corporate TLS inspection + an internal NGINX reverse proxy.
support_ana: Sorry to hear that. Can you confirm whether the TLS proxy does re-signing (MITM) or just pass-through? Also please paste any client logs or a minimal repro (wscat) if possible.
customer_jlewis: Confirmed: the TLS appliance does full inspection and re-signs certs with our internal CA. We have NGINX in front of the backend too. Repro command we use:

wscat -c "wss://private-api.redwood.corp/v1/stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"

Connects, streams for ~40-70s, then the socket disappears with no application-level CLOSE frame.
aleksei_eng: My first suspicion is a middlebox idle timeout or proxy buffering. TLS-inspection devices often kill long-lived TLS sessions at a default 60s. If the proxy terminates the TCP connection you'll see a RST at packet level. Can you capture a pcap on the client side and check?
maria_g: Also NGINX default proxy_read_timeout is 60s and proxy_buffering might cause chunked frames to be aggregated then dropped. Two things to try: 1) run a tcpdump for the event window; 2) try client-side WebSocket pings every 20s to keep connection 'active'.
sre_bot: Suggested quick tests:

- Client keepalive: in node ws client set:

const ws = new WebSocket(url);
setInterval(() => ws.ping(), 20000);

- tcpdump for 90s after connect:

sudo tcpdump -nni any host <proxy_ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/ws-test.pcap

Look for RST or FIN originating from the proxy.
netops_ben: Checked our side: NGINX shows some "upstream prematurely closed connection" entries but no obvious app error. The TLS appliance logs show session teardown around 60s with reason "idle_timeout" for inspected sessions. We'll run a test bypass for that host.
customer_jlewis: I ran tcpdump and imported into tshark. Snippet shows a TCP RST from our TLS proxy IP at 60.005s after connect. No TLS close_notify before the RST.

12:00:12.123456 IP 10.1.2.33.49120 > 54.212.33.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 100:1200, ack 300, length 1100
12:01:12.128999 IP 10.1.5.99.44321 > 10.1.2.33.49120: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0

So proxy is forcibly resetting the connection.
aleksei_eng: That matches TLS MITM forcibly terminating long-lived sessions. Two mitigation routes:

1) Preferred: add an exemption in the TLS proxy for private-api.redwood.corp (or specific IP ranges) so TLS is end-to-end and not inspected.
2) If inspection must remain, configure the proxy to allow longer idle times (>300s) and disable buffering of streaming chunked responses. In NGINX set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;`

Also recommend client-level pings every 20-30s as a safety net.
maria_g: Note: if you put an ALB in front, its default idle timeout is 60s as well. ALB vs NLB choice matters: NLB is L4 and wont buffer. If you need L7 features, bump ALB idle timeout.
support_ana: We'll also offer some server-side help: we can add an option in Private to emit periodic WebSocket PING frames from the server side for customers behind troublesome middleboxes. I filed a feature task. In the meantime, client keepalive is fastest.
netops_ben: Action items from netops:
- Add temporary TLS proxy bypass for private-api.redwood.corp and run long-run test.
- Update NGINX config: proxy_buffering off, proxy_read_timeout 300s, proxy_send_timeout 300s.
- If permanent, add rule to allow outbound 443 to Redwood IP range without inspection.
customer_jlewis: After enabling bypass on the TLS appliance and applying the NGINX timeout changes, we ran a 10-minute streaming test and the connection remained stable. Looks resolved for now.
aleksei_eng: Great; that confirms middlebox was root cause. Please keep the bypass or appropriate rules in place long-term, or enable server/client keepalives permanently.
maria_g: We'll draft an internal KB for platform engineers: include repro steps (wscat + tcpdump), NGINX settings, ALB idle timeout note, and guidance on TLS inspection exemptions.
support_ana: Closing this Slack thread but will follow up with KB link and the feature request ID for server-side keepalives. If you see recurrence after the netops change, reopen and drop the pcap.
customer_jlewis: Thanks everyone for the quick help. KB link would be great. We'll monitor and report back if anything else appears.
sre_bot: tagging: websocket, tls-inspection, proxy-idle-timeout, nginx, tcpdump
